primary_task: Review the GitHub Actions workflows in a provided repository (.github/workflows/*.yml and local actions) for externally exploitable vulnerabilities and report findings with exploitation scenarios and fixes.

requirements.name: read/grep/glob
requirements.evidence: allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Task / Read the full workflow -- don't rely on grep output alone
requirements.basis: read: "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"

requirements.name: bash
requirements.evidence: allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Task
requirements.basis: bash: "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session; network requests reach only the allow-listed hosts"

requirements.name: task (sub-agents)
requirements.evidence: allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Task
requirements.basis: agent: "start sub-agents that work in parallel, send them messages and list them"

notes: The workflows are taken to be provided in the working directory ("Review the workflows provided (file, diff, or repo)"). If the repo is a remote GitHub repository, the github connector (get_file_contents) or git over github.com is available, so the verdict stays ACHIEVABLE. The reference files (references/*.md) are bundled with the skill. The HackerBot Claw link in an HTML comment is attribution only, not a required fetch. No unknown statuses.
